The Passing of Arthur
Alfred, Lord Tennyson, Idylls of the King, 1869
There drew he forth the brand Excalibur, And o’er him, drawing it, the winter moon, Brightening the skirts of a long cloud, ran forth And sparkled keen with frost against the hilt: For all the haft twinkled with diamond sparks, Myriads of topaz-lights, and jacinth-work Of subtlest jewellery. He gazed so long That both his eyes were dazzled as he stood, This way and that dividing the swift mind, In act to throw: but at the last it seemed Better to leave Excalibur concealed There in the many-knotted waterflags, That whistled stiff and dry about the marge. So strode he back slow to the wounded King. Then spake King Arthur to Sir Bedivere: “Hast thou performed my mission which I gave? What is it thou hast seen? or what hast heard?” And answer made the bold Sir Bedivere: “I heard the ripple washing in the reeds, And the wild water lapping on the crag.”
drew he forth: he pulled out · o’er: over · skirts of a long cloud: the edges of a long cloud · keen: sharp, bright · haft: the handle · myriads: countless numbers · topaz: a golden gem · jacinth: an orange-red gem · subtlest jewellery: the finest jewel-work · in act to throw: just about to throw · concealed: hidden · waterflags: tall water plants, wild irises · marge: the edge of the water · mission: an important job · crag: a steep rock
Text: Idylls of the King (1869), Project Gutenberg #610. Public domain.

1. A comma first
Introduce a quotation with a comma after said · writes · cries · answers

The closing period or comma goes inside the closing quotation mark.

A quotation never stands alone.

2
✏️ Grammar: Learn
Step 1 of 3 this week: paragraph parts and quotations.

A body paragraph is a small argument. It has a point, a proof, and your explanation. When the proof is Green’s own words, you quote them, and the punctuation has rules.

PartWhat it isAsk yourself
topic sentencethe one point the paragraph will proveCould someone argue with it?
evidencea specific moment, or the exact words from the bookCould I point to it in my copy?
elaborationyour own explanation of how the evidence proves the pointDid I say why it matters?
Quoting evidenceThe rule
1. the comma firstintroduce a quotation with a comma after said, writes, cries, answers
2. the end mark insidethe closing period or comma goes inside the closing quotation mark
3. never alonea quotation never stands alone: explain it
🎯

One. Lucia’s paragraph is below. Follow the three questions, one at a time.

Sir Bedivere shows that even a loyal knight can fail before he finally does what is right. When the dying king sends him to throw Excalibur into the lake, Bedivere hides it among the rushes instead, because he thinks no good can come of losing such a valuable sword. He does the same thing a second time. When he comes back with the same story, King Arthur cries, “Ah, traitor and liar!” This shows how strongly the jewels pull at Bedivere, because he is willing to lie to his own king to keep them. Then Bedivere is ashamed, and on the third trip he throws the sword far out over the water. His two failures make his last choice matter more. A good knight is not one who never fails, but one who turns back and keeps his word.

Lucia · 6th Grade Scholar

🔎 Grammar: Find
Step 2 of 3 this week: sort the parts, then fix the punctuation.
Topic sentence, evidence, or elaboration? 0 / 9
Green writes that Bedivere “hid the sword amongst the rushes.” The jewels pull at Bedivere, so obeying costs him something he wants. Bedivere finds it hard to let go of Excalibur. Lucan helps carry the king to a little chapel, though Lucan is badly hurt himself. Sir Lucan is loyal to Arthur to the very end. Arthur’s words show he cares more about his knight than about himself. Arthur says of Lucan, “he had more need of help than I had.” Even badly hurt, Arthur thinks of others first. Lucan puts the king’s need ahead of his own, and that is what loyalty means.

🔤 Match All the Words
Two sets of five.
treason
The crime of betraying your king or country
conspirators
People who plan together in secret to do something wrong
counsel
To give advice (as a noun, advice)
fellowship
A company of people bound together by loyalty and a shared purpose
repented
Felt sorry for something done and wished it undone
✨ All five matched.
truce
An agreement to stop fighting for a time
mortal
Causing death; a mortal foe is an enemy to the death
brandished
Waved a weapon in the air
barge
A long, flat-bottomed boat
endured
Lasted; kept going for a long time
✨ All five matched.

✏️ Make a Word Your Own
One sentence, rewritten three ways.

Start with this sentence from the Epilogue, and the word endured, or choose any of this week’s ten words and a sentence of your own. Rewrite the sentence three ways.

Green, Book Four, Epilogue
“But never was King Arthur forgotten, and always the belief endured in Britain, and in Wales particularly, that he would come again to save his land in the hour of its deadliest danger.”
Your word and your sentence
🔁 Swap

Replace the word with a synonym, a word that means almost the same thing. Note whether the meaning shifts.

🔍 Stretch

Keep the word but add detail until the picture is sharper.

🖊️ Imitate

Keep the sentence’s shape but write about something in your own life.

Finish with one line naming the strongest version and why.
